key_insight: Decision-focused learning turns neural scores into fast multistage repair decisions, achieving the lowest evaluated costs when repair budgets bind.
engineering_relevance: The approach can support rapid power-network repair scheduling under uncertain, time-varying failures and limited repair capacity.
method: Predict scores for the sub-decision that drives state transitions.
Train on offline single-scenario solutions using a Fenchel–Young loss with perturbed optimization oracles.
Exploit structural conditions under which the targeted sub-decision enters the stage objective linearly.
evidence_signal: On synthetic 5-bus and IEEE 14-bus networks evaluated on common paths, budget-constrained DFL costs were 14%–23% below the next-best policy; on the 5-bus network, costs were within 1.8% of the exact optimum.
watch_item: Benefits depend on problem structure and operating constraints: without a repair budget, DFL did not outperform near-sighted MPC on the 14-bus network.
paper_title: Decision-Focused Learning for Multistage Stochastic Programs, with Application to Power Network Repair Scheduling
